question: Can a small model learn to estimate how well its own actual ordinary answer will do, and can it use that estimate when choosing one review? Keep a distinction between being wrong now and a review producing a useful future change.
body: Same six original uniform 8k memory experts with their own real-time recurrent activity and local edits. Inherit their bodies intact during this isolated five-coefficient readout fit; test without refit on the independent cohort and repaired bodies. Four real informative study contacts; 2/8 object loads reserved for transfer.
procedure: Give each offered odor two actual sequential five-tick orientations in random candidate order. The body makes a tentative ordinary choice on the second orientation of each, then receives three proprioception ticks without any taste or write. The environment records both actual choices. After the life one uniformly selected tentative choice is paid/scored, but no tentative result reaches the living graph before the review decision. Then the body chooses one physical revisit, eats the true taste on the chosen side, writes normally, and its single final ordinary action is actually scored.
readout: An affine three-parameter predictor on the two preceding motor logits, aligned to the actually chosen orientation/side, estimates the probability that that choice pays. At the review menu, evaluate this same predictor for the two possible own ordinary moves and average with its native motor probabilities. The two resulting per-candidate estimates remain only through the review decision. Two learned coefficients combine their right-minus-left difference and the native menu drive. There is no fixed sign that prefers low confidence. The procedure adds a small decision/forecast interface, not a stored table of true answers.
arms: All three use only realized final reward for on-policy choice credit and execute exactly one review. Forecast also fits its early probability to that life's one randomly scored tentative action using binary log loss. Uncredited performs and logs the same early action but does not use its score for prediction learning. Shuffled fits the same log loss to a different independent world's early payout, preserving the marginal outcome, sides and count. The inherited action-producing bodies are fixed in this assay so the auxiliary cannot make early answers purposely wrong.
budget: Three independent original-cohort training streams 1723721/1723727/1723741 per arm; 4000 updates, four new worlds per each of six bodies with eight candidate law variations, 32 actually chosen continuations per body/update. Adam .015, same initialization, matched choices' public clocks, small entropy / weight regularization. Strict new evaluation world seeds 2721577/2721581, 384 roots for the four-object task. Report forecast Brier and actual terminal success separately, one-body counterfactual side/random under equal budget, and the loss if privately experienced signals are donated from another history.
